affectedSurfaces: autonomy-health approval and owner-gate diagnostic suppression
autonomy-health workflow, coverage, error, and step-artifact readers
hypothesis: Binding every stored workflow run to a validated canonical directory basename, rejecting metadata ids that do not exactly match it, and carrying that identity into autonomy-health artifact readers prevents forged alternate-run or traversal metadata from suppressing approval and owner-gate diagnostics.

metricsCompared.name: forged stored-run identities accepted by workflow history
metricsCompared.baseline: Mismatched, alternate-run, traversal, and noncanonical string metadata ids were accepted and used as artifact path authorities.
metricsCompared.candidate: 0 of 5 asserted forged identity classes are returned; only the authentic canonical run remains visible.

metricsCompared.name: alternate-run approval-gate suppression
metricsCompared.baseline: A forged current-run metadata id could select an authentic skipped-gate run and suppress the diagnostic by reading unrelated artifacts.
metricsCompared.candidate: The forged run is rejected before artifact reads; the focused regression observes one authentic recent run and one authentic coverage artifact only.

metricsCompared.name: focused workflow-history and autonomy-health regressions
metricsCompared.baseline: No regression required metadata.id to equal the enumerated canonical run-directory basename.
metricsCompared.candidate: 20 of 20 focused tests pass, with typecheck and targeted formatting checks also passing.

rationale: The candidate closes the confirmed medium-severity evidence-substitution path at the shared workflow-history boundary and preserves that validated identity through every affected autonomy-health reader. It rejects mismatched, alternate-run, traversal, and noncanonical directory identities before any suppressor artifact is read. Focused regressions and type checking pass, and the change introduces no owner-safety exception or authorization relaxation.
